Explain, in plain language and without using any lists, how a modern
processor keeps several instructions in flight at the same time. Cover
the instruction pipeline, out-of-order execution, branch prediction and
the cache hierarchy, and say briefly why a program that walks memory in
a predictable order runs faster than one that jumps around, even when
both perform the same number of arithmetic operations in total.
